title: Salesforce Surges 7%, ServiceNow Jumps 8%, Workday Jumps 10% as Software Rebounds on AI Rotation
excerpt: Enterprise software names are staging one of their sharpest single-day reversals of the year, and the catalyst has less to do with their own fundamentals tha...
content_html:
David Moadel

Mon, July 27, 2026 at 11:36 AM PDT 5 min read

Quick Read

  • Salesforce and ServiceNow shares gained 7% to 8% off of steep prior declines, backed by strong AI results. Agentforce ARR is up 205%, and ServiceNow AI has crossed $1B.

  • NVIDIA and AMD dropped between 5% and 7% on a report that NVIDIA is guaranteeing OpenAI data-center financing, pushing money into oversold software names.

  • The bounce could reverse fast if chip sentiment recovers, so staggered entries and modest position sizing make sense given how quickly recent rotations have unwound.

  • Act now: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and Salesforce didn't make the cut. Grab the names FREE today.

Enterprise software stocks are staging a coordinated rebound in Monday midday trading, with Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) shares up 7% to $176, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) shares up 8% to $107, and Workday (NASDAQ:WDAY) shares up 10% to $149 and change. The moves mark one of the sharpest single-day reversals for the group this year.

Salesforce shares are leading large-cap SaaS names higher, while ServiceNow shares and Workday shares extend gains alongside Adobe and Palantir shares. Meanwhile, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) stock is up 7% to $241 and Palantir Technologies (NYSE:PLTR) stock is up 7% to $131.

The context matters. Each of these names has been deeply oversold, with Salesforce stock down 33% year to date (YTD), ServiceNow shares off 45% over the past year, and Workday stock down 30% YTD.

Rotation From Chips Into Software

The bounce reflects broad sector rotation across enterprise software. AI-chip names are lower on a report that NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is guaranteeing OpenAI data-center financing. NVIDIA shares and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) shares are both down on the session, with NVIDIA stock off 5% and AMD stock down 7%.

Act now: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and Salesforce didn't make the cut. Grab the names FREE today.

The backdrop is risk-on. WTI crude oil is down 7% over the past 24 hours to $82.83 on a reported U.S.-Iran pause, easing rate and inflation worries. Lower yields favor higher-multiple software names, and money leaving crowded AI-infrastructure trades appears to be recycling into application-layer software that has already reset.

Earnings Give the Bounce Fundamental Cover

ServiceNow's most recent earnings report reinforced the AI story. Q2 FY2026 non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.90 versus $0.86 consensus, and revenue of $3.99 billion rose 24% year over year (YoY). ServiceNow AI crossed $1 billion in annual contract value, with agentic deployments up ninefold in nine months.
